metadata.title: China Market Crash: The Reflexive Cascade

canonical_sources.title: China's stock market sinks into bear territory as CSI 300 extends 10-week rout
Chinese Stocks Tumble Into Bear Market as $2.4 Trillion Vanishes
In China, the AI bubble has already burst

pedagogy.problem_statement: China's benchmark CSI 300 plunged over 20% from its June 2026 peak, erasing over $2.4 trillion in market valuation across ten consecutive weekly drops. The underlying breakdown is a reflexive deleveraging spiral where property debt, margin liquidations, and retail panic reinforce one another.
pedagogy.core_thesis: China's equity crash is governed by reflexive deleveraging: under high leverage, price declines breach margin thresholds, triggering forced liquidations that retail-heavy trading (90% of volume) rapidly accelerates into an automated feedback loop.
pedagogy.mental_model: A synchronized financial domino cascade where an initial macro shock trips leverage gauges into automatic liquidations, triggering price drops that topple successive retail tiers.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: While a 20% drawdown defines a bear market, leverage ratio L mathematically wipes out 100% of collateral when prices fall by 1/L; with 90% retail participation, liquidation velocity scales hyper-linearly.
verified_claims: A 20% peak-to-trough decline defines bear-market territory; the CSI 300 crossed this boundary after 10 consecutive weekly routs in 2026.
With leverage ratio L (total exposure / equity), a price decline of approximately 1/L eliminates all equity collateral and triggers mandatory broker liquidation.
Retail investors account for roughly 90% of daily trading volume in China's equity markets compared to 20-25% in the US, amplifying procyclical panic selling.
Systemic stabilization requires real corporate earnings repair and confidence, as state ETF intervention alone cannot permanently arrest a reflexive solvency cascade.
anti_patterns: Do not treat headline GDP growth prints as proof of market solvency; equity re-pricing leads macroeconomic indicators.
Do not assume state-backed National Team ETF purchases alone halt liquidations without underlying credit restoration.
Do not confuse a temporary liquidity squeeze with an underlying balance-sheet deleveraging cycle.

scene_blueprint.title: The 20% Bear Threshold
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Establish the $2.4 trillion rout as the CSI 300 breaches the 20% bear market boundary after 10 weekly drops.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Index curve plunges downwards, crossing the 20% bear-market line as red alerts flash and $2.4T metric counts up.

scene_blueprint.title: The Leverage Wipeout
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Demonstrate that under leverage L, a fractional decline of 1/L wipes out 100% of collateral, triggering automated margin calls.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Leverage ratio meter expands to 3x while collateral level evaporates, detonating automated margin call alerts.

scene_blueprint.title: Retail Contagion Spiral
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Show how China's 90% retail trading share accelerates liquidations into a rapid reflexive feedback loop.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Swarm of retail particle flows cascades down, overwhelming buy liquidity and driving an accelerating reflexive price spiral.

scene_blueprint.title: Macro Shocks & Rebound
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Contrast state ETF intervention with the fundamental macro shocks of property debt, deflation, and corporate earnings repair.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Macro pressure nodes pulse red against state liquidity shields, highlighting that sustainable stabilization requires true earnings recovery.
